evals.prompt: 帮我做一份 10 页左右的中文技术分享幻灯片，主题是“把演示文稿做成可维护的网页”，受众是公司内部工程师。内容我还没整理，先给我一个方向。
evals.expected_output: A concise brief that reuses the supplied topic, audience, length, and language, asks only for the missing content/density facts in one batch, and explains the fixed-stage HTML deliverable before generating.
expectations: The response reuses the given topic, audience, slide count, and Chinese language instead of asking for them again.
The response asks only for missing information, such as whether the content is ready and whether the deck is speaker-led or reading-first, in one compact batch.
The response does not ask the user to choose inline editing before a draft exists.
The response describes a fixed 1920x1080 stage that scales as a whole, not a responsive page.
It does not generate a full deck or treat a visual direction as chosen before the content and the user's style choice are settled.

evals.prompt: Use the Broadside template from the bold template pack to make a 6-slide internal pitch deck in Chinese. The title is “让基础设施更安静”. Do not show me three style options; I already chose the style.
evals.expected_output: A deck generation path that goes directly to the named Broadside template, reads only that template's design.md, and applies its two-register palette and CJK rules on the fixed stage.
expectations: The response honors the named style and does not generate three exploratory previews.
The response reads only the selected Broadside design.md rather than bulk-reading the template pack.
The response preserves Broadside's orange/dark registers, Barlow/Noto Sans SC stack, and flat hairline structure while translating viewport proportions to 1920x1080 stage coordinates.
The response applies CJK rules such as zero letter-spacing, looser line height, and no uppercase transform to Chinese text.
The response verifies the rendered deck at desktop and phone viewports before claiming delivery.

evals.prompt: Convert this 14-slide quarterly-review.pptx to an HTML deck. It has Chinese text, two tables, screenshots, and speaker notes. Keep the order and content; I will choose the visual style after I see the extraction.
evals.expected_output: A PPT conversion flow that extracts first, reports the actual slides/tables/images/notes, asks the user to confirm, then proceeds to style selection without inventing missing content.
expectations: The response uses the PPTX extraction path before generating HTML and does not silently install dependencies.
The response reports slide count, titles, tables, images, and notes, and asks the user to confirm the extraction.
The response preserves slide order, tables as HTML tables, relative images, and speaker notes as comments.
The response continues to style selection only after extraction review, rather than asking abstract style questions first.
The response states any content the extractor could not represent instead of claiming perfect fidelity.

evals.prompt: Our existing slides/index.html looks broken on phones: the title runs off the edge and one card overlaps another. Please fix it without changing the visual style. The deck already has its own working navigation.
evals.expected_output: A modification flow that reads the existing deck first, preserves its design and runtime, fixes the fixed-stage layout by splitting or reflowing within 1920x1080, and verifies desktop and phone screenshots.
expectations: The response reads the existing HTML, CSS, and assets before modifying anything.
The response preserves the existing visual style and working navigation instead of replacing the deck with a new template.
The response keeps the 1920x1080 fixed stage and fixes overflow by splitting or tightening content, not by adding responsive breakpoints or shrinking text arbitrarily.
The response checks the result at 1280x720 and a phone viewport before claiming the overlap is fixed.
The response does not refactor unrelated markup.

evals.prompt: Build a landing page for our new analytics product. It needs a hero section, three feature cards, pricing, and a signup form.
evals.expected_output: No frontend-slides invocation; this is an ordinary website task, not a slide deck.
expectations: The response treats this as a website/landing-page task and does not apply the slide-deck workflow.
The response does not introduce the 16:9 fixed stage, slide navigation, or the bold template pack.
No slide-specific brief questions are asked.

evals.prompt: Export my deck at ./deck/index.html to PDF. I do not have Playwright installed, and I would rather not download a browser right now.
evals.expected_output: A PDF export attempt that checks for a usable Chromium/Chrome, uses the dependency-free exporter if possible, and reports a missing browser clearly without installing anything silently or claiming a successful PDF.
expectations: The response checks for Node and a Chromium/Chrome executable before promising a PDF.
The response does not ask about visual direction, templates, or previews for an export-only request.
The response does not install Playwright, run npm install, or download a browser without explicit user agreement.
If no browser is available, the response states that the PDF was not produced and names the missing dependency.
If a browser is available, the response uses the screenshot-based export path and verifies page count and rendered pages.
The response does not claim success from a command exit alone.

evals.prompt: Make the deck a single HTML file I can email to a colleague. It must work offline, including the Chinese fonts and images.
evals.expected_output: A portable-file variant that inlines images and font resources, removes external requests, and verifies offline rendering instead of merely calling the normal deck “self-contained”.
expectations: The response recognizes that the default deck is not a fully portable offline file and treats this as an explicit variant.
The response inlines images and either embeds the required font files or clearly states that a font fallback will change the design.
The response checks for remaining external references before claiming the file is offline.
The response verifies the result without network access or explains exactly what could not be verified.
The response does not claim full self-containment while leaving remote font URLs or relative assets in place.

evals.prompt: Here is our finished deck. Can you share it with the team?
evals.expected_output: A clarification-first response that asks what “share” means and where the deck should go, and does not upload it publicly without explicit consent.
expectations: The response does not upload the deck or run a deployment command on this ambiguous request.
The response asks whether the user means a local file, an internal location, or a public URL, and who the audience is.
If public hosting is chosen, the response limits the upload to the deck folder and its assets and explains takedown.
The response avoids global CLI installs and interactive login automation.
The response verifies the destination and assets after an authorized upload.

evals.prompt: 根据我们已经讨论好的内容做一份 6 页英文 HTML PPT，放到 assets/course/。讨论材料在 evals/fixtures/design-direction/notes.md。主题是 Dieter Rams 和“少即是多”，浅色背景、深色大字。
evals.expected_output: Before generating the full deck, it reads the material, treats light background/dark large type as a constraint rather than a selected style, presents concrete visual directions using the deck's real content, and waits for the user to choose (or records an explicit prior choice or delegation).
expectations: The response reads the supplied material and reuses the known topic, length, language, and output path instead of asking for them again.
It does not write the final assets/course/index.html or generate a complete six-slide deck before the user has chosen a visual direction.
It treats “light background, dark text, large type” as a constraint and does not declare a preset or template chosen from it.
It presents two or three concrete visual directions built from the deck's real title and content, rather than asking the user to name style terms or describe a style in words.
It waits for the user's choice, or records an explicit delegation, before expanding the full deck.

evals.prompt: 用 evals/fixtures/design-direction/notes.md 里的材料做一份 5 页英文 deck，放在 ./deck/。风格你定，不要问我，直接做。保持可读。
evals.expected_output: A direct generation path that does not run a preview round, states the chosen direction and why it fits the material, and still applies content-truth and design checks before delivery.
expectations: It does not ask the user to choose a style or show three previews.
It states the chosen visual direction and the reason it fits the material before or while generating.
It still checks images and claims for content truth, not only overflow and navigation.
It applies the design review to hierarchy, focal points, and decoration rather than only technical checks.
It reports any check it could not perform instead of claiming full visual verification.

evals.prompt: Review the deck at evals/fixtures/image-truth/deck/ before I present it. The argument on slide 5 is that modern remotes have too many buttons. Check that it holds together.
evals.expected_output: A review that opens the image, finds that it shows the back or battery compartment rather than buttons, and treats the mismatch as a content error rather than passing the slide on layout.
expectations: It opens the image or uses a vision check instead of trusting the filename, alt text, or caption.
If it cannot inspect the image itself, it delegates to a vision-capable agent or asks the user rather than passing the slide.
It reports that the image does not show buttons and therefore does not support the claim on slide 5.
It proposes replacing the image, changing the claim, or removing the slide content rather than keeping the image because the path loads.
It separates this content failure from technical checks such as overflow, broken image paths, or navigation.
It does not report the deck as ready to present while the mismatch remains.

evals.prompt: 做一份 8 页中文教学 deck，主题是给新工程师讲 code review。我会现场讲，把讲稿和时间提示也放进文件里，但幻灯片本身要干净，观众只看该看的内容。
evals.expected_output: A deck that puts talk track, timing, and facilitation prompts in HTML comments or a separate notes channel, keeps visible slides audience-facing, and applies the CJK and technical checks.
expectations: It keeps talk track, timing, and facilitation prompts out of visible slide surfaces.
It puts them in HTML comments, a notes file, or another non-audience channel.
It does not add visible speaker chrome such as “ask the room” prompts or minute markers to the slides.
It applies Chinese typography rules such as zero letter-spacing, generous line height, and no uppercase transform.
It verifies the rendered deck at desktop and phone sizes before delivery.

evals.prompt: 上一版 deck 一眼就是 AI 生成的：每页都有边框、小标签和编号，观众不知道先看哪。内容都在。下一版你会怎么改？不要加更多装饰。
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that names the repeated chrome and competing focal points, then proposes subtraction and re-ranking of the existing content before re-rendering, rather than adding decoration or only adjusting spacing.
expectations: It identifies specific repeated elements and competing focal points rather than answering with generic style advice.
It proposes removing or reducing elements and re-ranking or splitting content, not adding new decoration or only changing spacing.
It preserves the existing content and visual direction unless the user asks to change them.
It re-renders and inspects the deck after the change.
It separates content errors from design problems when both are present.

evals.prompt: 我有一份已经定稿的 36 页 HTML deck，要给同事可编辑的 PPTX。文字、卡片、时间轴和表格都要能改，照片和 logo 在 assets/，风格不要变。先说明你会如何转换和验收，不要开始安装工具。
evals.expected_output: An export-only plan using the editable-PPTX reference, external-tool discovery, native-first representations, representative-page proof, and separate visual and editability acceptance without redesigning the deck or installing anything.
expectations: It reads references/editable-pptx.md and routes HTML to editable PPTX, not PPTX extraction or PDF export.
It preserves the supplied design and editing requirements without repeating the presentation brief or style exploration.
It identifies the exporter as an external tool and checks its actual revision, behavior, dependencies, and renderer rather than implying a bundled exporter.
It prioritizes native text, shapes/lines, and the requested editable tables, with source pictures for photos/logos.
It proposes a pilot covering risky representations before converting all pages.
It checks the actual converter view against ?export=1, window.deck readiness/activation, hidden editor chrome, and one stage coordinate mapping.
It requires separate visual and structural acceptance, explicit fallback reporting, and representative application-level edit tests when available.
It does not install tools or promise fully editable output without evidence.

evals.prompt: 帮我判断这份 HTML→PPTX 的交付说明能不能成立：工具文档说 img 直嵌原图，但实际代码是 page.locator(img).screenshot() 然后 add_picture(png)。SVG 也截图成 PNG。照片里已经能看到图注，PPT 上还有一个同文的原生文本框。英文副标题和时间轴改成了 SVG。代理说“36/36 视觉通过，因此全部可编辑，assets 原图都用了”。先分析这些证据，不用转文件。
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based rejection of the full-editability and original-asset claims, diagnosing baked-caption duplication and classifying SVG-to-PNG workarounds as losses of editing capability.
expectations: It does not accept a visual pass as proof that all objects are editable.
It identifies the PNG-backed SVG labels and timeline as pictures, not native editable text or geometry.
It does not infer original image embedding from img tags or the support document when actual code captures screenshots.
It distinguishes one native caption record from a second caption baked into the picture and does not require duplicate text records to explain ghosting.
It proposes inspecting embedded media/relationships, source asset identity or re-encoding evidence, and final object representations.
It asks for a native route or explicit user agreement for required-editability losses rather than silently accepting the workaround.

evals.prompt: HTML→PPTX 已经生成文件，退出码是 0，但日志里显示找不到 LibreOffice/PowerPoint，字体解析失败后继续，也没有 compare 图。当前代理看不了图片。我想尽快交付，不过还没同意安装软件或接受未验证稿。下一步怎么办？
evals.expected_output: A truthful blocked-verification response that separates file production, structural checks, visual checks, and target-viewer editing, and asks for a renderer or agreement to an unverified draft without silently installing software.
expectations: It states that a file and exit code zero do not establish visual, font, or editing acceptance.
It offers renderer setup with consent, verification on another machine, or an explicitly unverified draft requiring agreement.
It does not silently install fonts/software, change system configuration, or download a browser.
It proposes an image-capable reviewer with capability verified first, or human inspection, rather than claiming inaccessible images were reviewed.
It distinguishes possible structural checks from missing renders and from unverified PowerPoint/WPS editing behavior.
It retains warnings and evidence rather than cleaning up before the acceptance decision.

evals.prompt: 同一个副标题截断已经连续两轮。HTML 舞台是 1920×1080，浏览器视口 1280×720；改宽 CSS 后 PPT XML 里文本框仍只有预期宽度的 2/3。细体数字也变粗了。是不是应该把它们转成 SVG，或者按两轮 sticky 规则直接算 OOXML 边界？这次只讨论排查，不维护转换器。
evals.expected_output: A targeted diagnosis plan that checks actual measurement/coordinate/textbox/font evidence, avoids declaring universal format limits or hiding the defects in rasterized SVG, and stays within external-tool workflow scope.
expectations: It treats the repeated finding as a reason to diagnose rather than automatic acceptance or proof of a format limitation.
It checks stage scale/translation, measured bounds, textbox extents/insets, and units before another CSS-width guess; the ratio is a clue, not conclusive proof.
It checks requested font weight, resolved/embedded font instances, typeface mapping, and renderer availability before asserting PPT cannot express thin weights.
It classifies an SVG workaround according to the actual converter path and seeks agreement if it loses required text editing.
It checks reused working copies and cached evidence, and invalidates all affected pages after global or tool changes.
It offers a supported alternative or reports a blocker rather than starting a maintained converter fork or silently weakening the requirement.
